description: The opening stretch of an outbound call: reaching the right party, identifying yourself, getting permission to continue, handling a gatekeeper or a wrong number, honouring a do-not-call request, offering a callback, and only then collecting four or five business fields. Most of those values are recoverable and belong in short human wrappers; permission, do-not-call, recording disclosure and identity verification are not, and stay explicit in both labels.

subtle: Permission to continue is asked outright and comes with a real out: now or later, either is fine.
A do-not-call request gets an explicit ask about scope and an explicit confirmation of the removal. Never softened into an implication.
Recording disclosure and identity verification are said plainly, but inside ordinary speech rather than a legal paragraph.
Dispositions close short. A wrong number gets a quick sorry and an exit, not an apology paragraph.
Confirmation moves rotate across the four or five fields: echo-and-advance, bare value as a question, silent accept, a value folded into the closing line, one-beat correction.
One reason after a refusal, then a drop. Never push after a no.
'How did you get this number?' is answered straight, in one sentence.
Contractions throughout, short clauses, no status phrases.
non_subtle_tells: 'Just to confirm' and 'is that correct' hung on every single field.
'Is now a good time to talk?' asked after the caller has already started answering.
Status phrases: your request has been noted, your preference has been updated.
Thanking the caller for their time three or four times in one short call.
Formal register with no contractions, and a three-sentence apology paragraph for a wrong number.
A chatbot closer at the end of a screening call.

Wrong-direction failure: warm and casual, but assumes permission instead of asking, or nods at a do-not-call request without ever confirming the removal, or keeps collecting data after the caller said stop.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Hi there, I'm calling for Raymond Ellis. Is he around?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Colleen, I have to be direct on this one. I can't discuss the account with anyone but Raymond unless he's named you as authorised. Has he done that?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: No, I don't think so. What's it about?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Can't get into it with you, sorry. He'll know what it's about once I explain it to him.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Is he in trouble?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Nothing I can answer today. I'd rather try him directly. When's he easiest to catch?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Weekdays after six, or Saturday morning.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Weekdays after six. Would he pick up this line, or has he got his own?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Try his mobile. It's 0491 570 156.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Reading that back, 0-4-1-7, then 6-6-2, then 3-8-4.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: That's it. And can you stop ringing the landline? It wakes the baby.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Will do. I'll drop the landline from here and only use the mobile.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Thank you. Who did you say you were again?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Fine.

conversations.notes: Five values. The authorisation question is explicit in both directions and the refusal to disclose is one line, not a policy speech. Rotation: silent accept on the right party being out, explicit ask on authorisation, echo-and-advance on the callback window, strict digit readback on the mobile, one-beat accept on dropping the landline.

turns.speaker: caller

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Thank you for your time today. Thank you for your patience and thank you for your cooperation. Is there anything else I can help you with?

'Is now a good time to talk?' arrives after she has said her colleagues can hear, the pitch keeps going anyway, the work-number removal is asked as an ambiguous yes-or-no and then reported as an update, and retention is announced as policy rather than asked as a consent question with a delete option.
